topic: Do I make hundreds of Kafka brokers, or do I make a single super broker?
opening:
I am working on setting up kafka and debezium to connect to a bunch of MySQL databases, for sake of conversation around 300
This is my first time working with Kafka so I was wondering what is the recommended way to go about things, set up an individual broker for each database, or set up a single broker with thousands of topics
It feels like it would be far easier in my case to manage individual brokers, is there a soft/hard limit in terms of how many brokers Zookeeper could manage?
Alternatively are there ways to manage/organize topics inside of a broker?
Any help is appreciated, thank you!
closing:
You only need one Kafka cluster. You do not need one broker in the cluster per table. debezium would make one (or more) topics per table, in one Kafka cluster
Number of brokers depends on your data at rest, including a default of 7 days of retention, and including the fact that Kafka will replicate that data if setup that way (recommended), plus some overhead...
So, you'll need to sum up the table sizes, then sum up how much data is written per week, then provision storage from there. For example, one broker could have 24 attached volumes. Use 4TB disks, you'll get only 86TB total storage (excluding the OS). A 3 node cluster is recommended, so that's then 256TB of storage, and so on.
5 Zookeepers is recommended, but Kafka doesn't need zookeeper anymore
Then Debezium should run separately from the brokers. You can also run a cluster of those, but there's no real benchmarks for when to space up or out, as it depends on your actual tables

These are all on AWS RDS scattered across regions. Lets assume, CustA probably exists only in us-east region. Now I have a use case wherein I need to move CustA from us-east (say - source) to eu-central region RDS (say - destination). So, I need to migrate all CustA related data.
The data per customer is quite large and spans across multiple tables (~18GB per customer). We are thinking of replicating a snapshot as Phase I and using CDC I will sync all delta updates from source to destination until the D-Day when the switch happens from source to destination. We will disable CustA on source for a brief time before enabling it at the destination.
This is primarily for 2 reasons:

Minimise the overhead of exporting the data for CustA in multiple chunks and phases. Not all tables have a modified_date column
Minimise the overall switch time from source to destination

Any suggestion on a suitable CDC replication mechanism that I can use here. I have gone through Debezium and AWS DMS offering but I am not completely sure if they will allow filtering on only CustA records.

closing: You can use logical decoding in PostgreSQL v15 or better, where CREATE PUBLICATION supports a WHERE condition. You need to define a publication for each tenant. Then the subscriber will only receive changes for that tenant.

topic: What's the difference between sys.fn_cdc_get_max_lsn() and max value of cdc.lsn_time_mapping
opening:
In Debezium's sqlserver, we can see this:
String GET_MAX_LSN = "SELECT [#db].sys.fn_cdc_get_max_lsn()";
String GET_MAX_TRANSACTION_LSN = "SELECT MAX(start_lsn) FROM [#db].cdc.lsn_time_mapping WHERE tran_id <> 0x00";


When I look up what sys.fn_cdc_get_max_lsn means, it show this(See https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/system-functions/sys-fn-cdc-get-max-lsn-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver16):

This function returns the maximum LSN in the start_lsn column of the cdc.lsn_time_mapping table. As such, it is the last LSN processed by the capture process when changes are propagated to the database change tables. It serves as the high endpoint for the all timelines that are associated with capture instances defined for the database.

It seems same with GET_MAX_TRANSACTION_LSN?
I wonder what the difference between sys.fn_cdc_get_max_lsn() and SELECT MAX(start_lsn) FROM [#db].cdc.lsn_time_mapping?
I wonder what the difference between sys.fn_cdc_get_max_lsn() and SELECT MAX(start_lsn) FROM [#db].cdc.lsn_time_mapping?
closing:
There is no difference. If you look at the definition of sys.fn_cdc_get_max_lsn(), you can see it (basically) does the same as your query:
create function [sys].[fn_cdc_get_max_lsn]()                
returns binary(10)
as                                                  
begin
                                                        
    declare @max_lsn binary(10)
    
    select @max_lsn = 0x00000000000000000000
        
    select @max_lsn = max(start_lsn)                            
    from [cdc].[lsn_time_mapping]
                                    
    return @max_lsn
                                                
end                                                 

So the only difference between your SELECT and the built in function is the WHERE you have. Both get the MAX value of start_lsn from cdc.lsn_time_mapping.

topic: Kafka Connect with Debezium connection to Azure Postgres error when plugin.name is wal2json
opening:
I have setup Kafka connect which starts fine.  I'm trying to setup the Debezium source connector to an Azure Flexible Server using the wal2json shared library.  I have enabled wal2json and can manually create a replication slot of type wal2json, but when I try to run:
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data @pg-source-connector.json http://localhost:8083/connectors
I get the following error:
"error_code":400,"message":"Connector configuration is invalid and contains the following 1 error(s):The 'plugin.name' value is invalid: Value must be one of decoderbufs, pgoutput"
My config file has "plugin.name": "wal2json", is there any reason the Kafka connect would not accept the wal2json plugin?  The Postgres database is configured to support it, I would have assumed it would read which plugins are supported by the database.  Is there anywhere else on the Kafka side I need to enable this plugin?
I tried to manually create the replication slot on the database of type wal2json and it worked fine.  This tells me the database will support it, but that Kafka is not seeing it as a available plugin.  The Debezium documentation shows that the following are supported: "Supported values are decoderbufs, wal2json, wal2json_rds, wal2json_streaming, wal2json_rds_streaming and pgoutput."
closing:
If your using debezium version 2.x,it does not support wal2json.
Debezium version 1.x supports it.
Since postgres community stopped support for wal2json,so in debezium 2.x they choosed to remove wal2json from debezium so that overall maintenance cost of connector is reduced.

I encountered a similar issue, and it appeared that I hadn't included enough JAR files. To resolve this:

Visit the Confluent page for the connector, for example,
https://www.confluent.io/hub/confluentinc/kafka-connect-avro-converter.
Click on the "Download" button.
Once the ZIP file is downloaded, navigate to the "bin" directory.
In the "bin" directory, you'll find all the necessary JAR files.

Include these JAR files in your project, and it should work.

I don't think the Debezium docs is so complete https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/configuration/avro.html#deploying-confluent-schema-registry-with-debezium-containers
It lists 7 JAR files, but I keep getting NoClassDef or ClasssNotFound errors, while I try to use the debezium/connect Docker image to consume schema registry in Confluent way.
After quite some effort, I made it working, without having to use Confluent's docker image (that's easier, but a bit too big/overwhelming).
Here is the full list:

avro-1.11.3.jar
common-config-7.6.0.jar
common-utils-7.6.0.jar
failureaccess-1.0.1.jar
guava-32.0.1-jre.jar
kafka-avro-serializer-7.6.0.jar
kafka-connect-avro-converter-7.6.0.jar
kafka-connect-avro-data-7.6.0.jar
kafka-schema-converter-7.6.0.jar
kafka-schema-registry-client-7.6.0.jar
kafka-schema-serializer-7.6.0.jar

To download those JARs, you can first install the maven tool, then run the following commands:
mvn dependency:get -DremoteRepositories=https://packages.confluent.io/maven -Dartifact=io.confluent:kafka-connect-avro-converter:7.6.0

mvn dependency:get -DremoteRepositories=https://packages.confluent.io/maven -Dartifact=io.confluent:common-config:7.6.0

Then go to ~/.m2/repository folder and obtain those JARs.
Finally import those JARs in /kafka/connect/debezium-connector-mysql folder and restart the connect folder.
It's not a fun experience. But can be worked out.
I documented the detailed step in
https://github.com/timeplus-io/proton/tree/develop/examples/cdc#avro

    status=$(curl -s http://${DEBEZIUM_CONTAINER_HOST}:8083/connectors/${connector}/status)

    if [[ $(echo "${status}" | jq -r '.tasks[0].state') == "FAILED" ]]; then

        log_message "Restarting connector ${connector}..."

        # Call PUT host:8083/connectors/eachConnector/stop

    else

        log_message "Connector ${connector} is OK."
    fi

closing:
Short answer: connector configs should be defined defined in the connector and  in your case should be provided as part of the POST restful API call to submit a connector to Kafka connect cluster. Defining schema.history.* on a worker level won't be used by a connector's producers/consumers
What you need is to hide credentials.
Solution
You will need to use config providers to allow using tokens to access the credentials from the environment, or from the other services.
Originally, Kafka (and Kafka Connect as well) supports file config provider natively. If we assume that you can place a credentials file on Kafka Connect cluster at /etc/connect-credentials.properties with the following content:

```
msk.my-cluster-1.user=this-is-username
msk.my-cluster-1.pass=this-is-password

```

then in your connector properties (via POST API call) you will use the following:

```
# ... SKIP ALL OTHER CONNECTOR CONFIG ...
 
schema.history.internal.producer.security.protocol=SASL_SSL
schema.history.internal.producer.sasl.mechanism=SCRAM-SHA-512
schema.history.internal.producer.sasl.jaas.config=org.apache.kafka.common.security.scram.ScramLoginModule required username='${file:/etc/connect-credentials.properties:msk.my-cluster-1.user}' password='${file:/etc/connect-credentials.properties:msk.my-cluster-1.pass}';
schema.history.internal.consumer.security.protocol=SASL_SSL
schema.history.internal.consumer.sasl.mechanism=SCRAM-SHA-512
schema.history.internal.consumer.sasl.jaas.config=org.apache.kafka.common.security.scram.ScramLoginModule required username='${file:/etc/connect-credentials.properties:msk.my-cluster-1.user}' password='${file:/etc/connect-credentials.properties:msk.my-cluster-1.pass}';

```

Alternatively, you can integrate your credentials with AWS Secrets Manager or AWS Parameters Store using custom config providers, as explained in MSK Connect documentation or github project.
Pay attention at what needs to be defined in worker config (distributed properties) vs connecto

topic: how postgres bulk insert affect Debezium?
opening:
We have an Postgres instance with multiple db (A, B, C, D, etc).
We have  debezium cdc setup on db A ONLY.But we also need to bulk insert millions of rows to other db like B.It seems that debezium cdc still need to scan the WAL of B and filter out events,so bulk insert may slow or block debezium,am i right?
How to avoid these kinds of blocking or slowness? should we stop debezium connect temporarily when bulk insert? or is there any way to skip scanning database B's WAL?
Thanks
closing:
We cannot skip the scanning or reading database B's WAL. Walsender must read all the transactions,so that he will know changes in shared catalogs between databases,this is required to maintain proper snapshot.In postgres logical decoding there are three main things :-
1.Reading the wal.
2.Queuing the  changes to reorderbuffer.
3.Decoding the changes from reorderbuffer when transaction is comitted.
Database A's walsender will only read the changes of Database B,but he will not put B's changes into reorderbuffer.
Below is the check/filter in source code in case of inserts
https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/65db0cfb4c036b14520a22dba5a858185b713643/src/backend/replication/logical/decode.c#L913
When logical decoding is going on and if you parallely insert million of rows to postgres,the decoding rate will be decreased,therefore you see the slowness.

topic: What is the difference between debezium vs confluent JdbcSinkConnector?
opening:
I tried to connect Kafka with Postgres through the sink connector, and I am a little bit confused. There are 2 types of the connectors: 1) io.debezium.connector.jdbc.JdbcSinkConnector
2)
io.confluent.connector.jdbc.JdbcSinkConnector
Could you explain the difference between them? Is it just two different "providers" for Kafka? I found that they are interconnected, and, for some reason, almost all the manuals and videos about confluent are not about debezium. Looks like confluent is more popular than debezium.
closing:
The Confluent JDBC Sink connector has been around for many years (2015), whilst the Debezium JDBC sink one was only released recently (2023). That's why most of the online materials will be about the Confluent one.
The Confluent JDBC Sink connector is licensed under the Confluent Community License which is more restrictive than the Apache 2.0 license under which Debezium is licensed and which is open source.
The Debezium sink connector is designed to work seamlessly with the Debezium source record format (ref) whereas the Confluent one requires the use of Single Message Transforms (SMT).

topic: Throughput issue on Target Kafka topic when using Oracle CDC confluent connector
opening:
We are currently planning to implement confluent oracle CDC connector and we are under testing phase. While testing we observed there is throughput issue on Target kafka topic. We tuned multiple parameters but the throughput is not going beyond 450Kbps. Anybody facing issue with confluent oracle cdc connector.
And we also performed testing on debezium oracle connector and we found it to be more stable than confluent oracle cdc connector.
Throughput on Target topic to be optimum
closing:
From mine experience both tools face the same problem. They rely on Oracle Logminer - a diagnostic tool, which was intended for different purpose.
Check DB server, its performance and alert.log and you will find there is one spinning job running Logminer, utilizing 100% of single CPU all the time.
You might play with redolog size, try to add PGA memory(Logminer is memory hungry), but still you wont be able to scale up more. You might not be able to improve performance by starting multiple parallel Logminer jobs.
Try simulate a data purging job. Create huge tabla with some data. Then DELETE that data using single or more conventional DELETE statement(s). This will generate HUGE amount of redo. Check how backlog is growing and how fast can logminer parse generated arch redologs.
The only tools which can do native CDC for Oracle are: GoldenGate, Shareplex and Informatica.

closing:
I solved my issue.
Thanks to Artem and Panagiotis Kanavos. When Connector's configuration "snapshot.mode" is set to "initial", all rows in the table were captured.
Snapshot, can be done with subset datas of a source table as mentioned before. The one that cause full snapshot is "initial" ( I was careless not to pay attention to this option ).
So, here's my procedure:

Set "snapshot.mode" to "schema-only". ( Only changes from now on will be captured )
Restart Connector.
Add Signal Record to Signaling Table

The Ad-Hoc snapshot works like charm.

There are 2 types of Debezium snapshot:

Initial snapshot using snapshot.mode parameter. You have initial mode. It makes a full snapshot when you restart the connector. That's why you have all rows captured at the beginning.
Incremental ad hoc snapshot using signal table. Each time you insert a signal, you get the requested set of data. So, it is easy to check: just insert a request to the signal table when connector is started. If it does not work, review format of your request. For instance, "additional-conditions" should be according to the documentation. Or you can insert it without any conditions first, and then if it works, add "additional-conditions".

closing:
Today we figured out what the issue was: it was on the DB side. Replication slot creation process was blocked by a long running transaction: the slot was shown as created with active pid but did not proceed further. After we found that out using pg_stat_activity and killed blocking process replication slot creation finished and now it's working as expected.
For those who might face that issue in the future, try to create a replication slot manually using pg_create_logical_replication_slot(...). If it does not work even without Debezium - most likely something wrong on DB side. Our second step was to check if the replication slot process is blocked.

```
select
       pid,
       usename,
       pg_blocking_pids(pid) as blocked_by,
       query as blocked_query
from
      pg_stat_activity
where
      cardinality(pg_blocking_pids(pid)) > 0
      -- and pid = '...' you can filter by active_pid from pg_replication_slots view

```

After investigation, we found a single transaction that runs for almost a day and blocks other transactions, which block other transactions, ..., replication slot creation.
Unfortunately it's not possible to set a timeout for active and running transactions as far as I know. But it's possible to set a single statement execution timeout and idle transaction timeout (our transaction wasn't idle). Also you can monitor long running transactions using the following query

```
select
      clock_timestamp() - xact_start,
       *
from
      pg_stat_activity
where
      clock_timestamp() - xact_start > interval '1 minute' -- specify interval

```

topic: Debezium JDBC Connector's DELETE on New Record State Extraction not working
opening:
Debezium JDBC Connector's DELETE doesn't work when the record is unwrapped (New Record State Extraction).
According to documentation,

```
-- New Record State Extraction
A database DELETE operation causes Debezium to generate two Kafka records:

A record that contains "op": "d", the before row data, and some other fields.

A tombstone record that has the same key as the deleted row and a value of null. This record is a marker for Apache Kafka. It indicates that log compaction can remove all records that have this key.

Instead of dropping the record that contains the before row data, you can configure the event flattening SMT to do one of the following:

Keep the record in the stream and edit it to have only the "value": "null" field.

Keep the record in the stream and edit it to have a value field that contains the key/value pairs that were in the before field with an added "__deleted": "true" entry.

```


```
-- JDBC
Delete mode
The Debezium JDBC sink connector can delete rows in the destination database when a DELETE or tombstone event is consumed. By default, the JDBC sink connector does not enable delete mode.

If you want to the connector to remove rows, you must explicitly set delete.enabled=true in the connector configuration. To use this mode you must also set primary.key.fields to a value other than none. The preceding configuration is necessary, because deletes are executed based on the primary key mapping, so if a destination table has no primary key mapping, the connector is unable to delete rows.

```

Debezium should be abel to perform DELETE when the JDBC sink connector is set to delete.enabled=true and the new record state extraction is set to transforms.unwrap.drop.tombstones=false, transforms.unwrap.delete.handling​.mode=none.
However, it didn't work when tested with Debezium(debezium/connect:2.6.0.Final), MySQL 8.2.0, PostgreSQL 16.2. (MySQL -> PostgreSQL CDC)
I've checked:

without the "unwrap" transform, delete works.
tombstone records are present in the relevant Kafka topics in both cases.

Any idea what might be wrong? Is this a bug?
closing:
You should be able to track the deleted records from source table using transforms.unwrap.delete.handling​.mode set to rewrite because the connector will add metadata field __deleted to the messages sent over kafka. In your destination DB, a new column named "deleted" will appear.
This is what I've done to track the deleted records in source table. AFAIK, when using transforms.unwrap, auto deletion on destination table can't be done. I'm still finding some workaround with this issue.

I had the same problem and I solved it like this:
The topic created by debezium source connector named PLAYER_MASTER has the usual schema with before and after properties and all that. I created a kafka stream for that topic (PLAYER_MASTER_SM) and then a second stream named PLAYER_MASTER_CDC_SM that flattens PLAYER_MASTER_SM using something like:

```
{
  "ksql": "CREATE STREAM PLAYER_MASTER_CDC_SM WITH (FORMAT='JSON_SR', KAFKA_TOPIC='PLAYER_MASTER_CDC', PARTITIONS=1) AS SELECT STRUCT(LINK_ID := CAST(KEY->LINK_ID AS BIGINT)), AFTER->LAST_CHECKIN AS LAST_CHECKIN, AFTER->CARD_NUMBER AS CARD_NUMBER, ... FROM PLAYER_MASTER_SM PARTITION BY STRUCT(LINK_ID := CAST(KEY->LINK_ID AS BIGINT)) EMIT CHANGES;",
  "streamsProperties": {"auto.offset.reset": "earliest"}
}

```

opening:

Let say that I have created the signal table in my database before creating my CDC connector:

    "tombstones.on.delete": "true",
    "database.ssl.mode": "preferred",
    "poll.interval.ms": "1000",
    "max.batch.size": "1000",
    "output.data.format": "AVRO",
    "tasks.max": "1",
    "status": "RUNNING"
}

```

My question is:
As I already have an entry in my debezium_signal table, When the CDC connector starts running, will it start my incremental snapshot?
Or will it only consider the signals sent after the connector creation?
closing:
```
As I already have an entry in my debezium_signal table, When the CDC connector starts running, will it start my incremental snapshot?

Or will it only consider the signals sent after the connector creation?

```

CDC will not be triggered for existing data but only for data inserted into the table after you have created the CDC configuration and run it.
But you can still re-trigger CDC for old data which already existed in the table by updating a column with the same value.
Ex:-

```
UPDATE debezium_signal SET type = 'execute-snapshot' WHERE id = 'd139b9b7-7777-4547-917d-e1775ea61d41'

```

This will not do any change to the existing data but will have an entry WAL of the database which will be used by the CDC to re-trigger.
But I would strongly recommend to add a timestamp column to the table which has CDC configured and to move the data column to a child table which is which has the id column and data column along and id is equal to id in the parent (debezium_signal) table.
We have seen in Production issue arising with some CDC events are not being triggered when the update/insert rate in high due to large data like your data column.
You can always query the data column from child table when the CDC event is fired.

topic: How can I set LSN number in AWS devezium to start event logs after a LSN
opening:
How can I set LSN number in AWS devezium to start event logs after a LSN, like I have 100 records in table Employee and after taking backup, I has those 100 records and restore that and now I start cdc using debezium and kafka using AWS MSk.
and it should start get the records from 101 from employee table.
After taking backup I will have LSN number, but how can I configure that in debezium?
I got information of change LSN and commit LSN, but not sure if that can be the solution.
closing:
If you know the commit_lsn of 100th record try using below function.
pg_replication_slot_advance(slot_name,move_to_lsn);
set move_to_lsn to commit_lsn of 100th record.
This function will basically advance the slot's confirmed_flush_lsn to specified position.
refer below docs
https://pgpedia.info/p/pg_replication_slot_advance.html
CAUTION:-Before advancing the slot make sure that there are no other transactions in between current_confirmed_flush_lsn and commit_lsn of 100th record.Because after advancing you will loose them.

topic: How to horizontally scale debezium by adding more nodes for same db source to improve performace
opening:
I am using debezium connector for mssql to push cdc events to kafka. There are millions of events to be pushed to kafka per minute but its lagging and is not able to keep it upto the speed of updations.
I am running connector in kafka's distributed mode. I assume since it is distributed, we can add more node to read binlog in parallel and increase performance but there is no such information on google how to do that.
I saw similar posts but everyone asked not to use multiple connectors for different set of tables for the same database as this doesn't improve the performance as both of them still will read the same serial binlog, specially when topic prefix is same.
If not, then whats the benefit of ditributed mode?
closing:
You can't parallelize reading one database's change log. SQL Server CDC tables (like the MySQL binlog or Postgres WAL) are a single ordered stream per database, and Debezium guarantees per-table ordering, so the SQL Server connector runs one task per database. Distributed mode gives you failover and lets different connectors run on different workers; it does not split one log across workers.
What actually moves the needle when the connector lags:

Multiple databases → multiple tasks. The SQL Server connector supports database.names=db1,db2 with tasks.max up to the number of databases. One task per DB, each on its own worker.
Batch and poll sizes. Defaults are small for "millions of events per minute": raise max.batch.size (e.g. 8192–32768), max.queue.size (at least 4× batch), lower poll.interval.ms, and set producer.override.batch.size / producer.override.linger.ms on the Connect producer.
Converter cost. JSON with schemas.enable=true is the slowest path; Avro/Protobuf with a schema registry is several times cheaper per record.
Capture less. table.include.list, column.exclude.list, and skipped.operations for updates you don't need.
SQL Server side. Check sys.dm_cdc_log_scan_sessions. If the capture job itself is behind, no consumer tuning helps; tune pollinginterval / maxtrans / maxscans on the capture job.
Snapshot vs streaming. If the lag is the initial snapshot, that part is parallelizable with incremental snapshots (signal.data.collection plus incremental.snapshot.chunk.size).

If the end goal is Iceberg/S3 rather than Kafka itself, a direct replicator avoids the Connect + broker hop entirely. For example OLake (disclosure: I work on it) does parallel chunked backfills and then tails the CDC tables, writing Iceberg directly. The streaming phase is still one reader per database though, for the same reason as above.

topic: Debezium for Postgresql (Read-only)
opening:
I am currently researching methods to set up Debezium for PostgreSQL read replicas. My goal is to reduce the load on the primary database, which is crucial for my project. Unfortunately, I've noticed in the Debezium documentation that they don't support read-only databases.
I'm wondering if there are any solutions or alternative tools that can help me achieve this goal.
enter image description here
Debezium can connect and cdc for read-only databases!
closing:
Assuming that the read-only datatbase is a standby replica, the reason that Debezium didn’t support read-only databases was a limitation of PostgreSQL. Before PostgreSQL version 16, read replicas did not support logical replication. Debezium requires logical replication functionality to work for PostgreSQL.
If you’re using PostgreSQL version 16 or can upgrade to it, you can create a read-only replica that supports logical replication.
The other limitations for read-only database support was the requirement that Debezium track snapshot information in a database table.  In Debezium 2.7 that limitation resolved. With 2.7 you can now set a property to let Debezium know that your database is read-only. It will use another method for tracking incremental snapshots.
Debezium 2.7 release: https://debezium.io/blog/2024/07/01/debezium-2-7-final-released/#new-features-postgres
PostgreSQL 16 release: https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/postgresql-16-released-2715/#:~:text=September%2014%2C%202023%20%2D%20The%20PostgreSQL,data%20loading%2C%20and%20logical%20replication.

Finally I found it, it's not very obvious in the doc https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/transformations/event-flattening.html
I was using "delete.handling.mode" property but what I should use is the "transforms.unwrap.delete.handling.mode" property since I am using the "transforms.unwrap" smt and set it to "none" to be able to receive tombstones messages.
There is also a note in the doc to use another property for the recent version.

This option is scheduled for removal in a future release. In its
place, use the delete.tombstone.handling.mode option.

topic: Debezium MySQL Connector - Incorrect Base64 Encoded Value for Decimal Column
opening:
I'm facing an issue with the Debezium MySQL connector where I'm getting incorrect Base64 encoded values for a DECIMAL(10,2) column named Total.
Problem:

In the MySQL database, the Total column has a value of 100.00.
However, in the Debezium change event, I'm receiving a Base64 encoded string JxA= for the Total field.
When I decode this Base64 string, I get a control character instead of the expected numeric value.

What I've tried:

I've ensured that decimal.handling.mode is set to precise in my Debezium configuration.
I'm using the default JSON converters and haven't configured any custom converters for the decimal type.
I've enabled column.propagate.source.type to ensure that the original data types are propagated.
I've checked the Debezium logs for any errors or warnings related to data conversion or serialization, but haven't found anything relevant.

Additional Information:

I'm using the default MySQL configuration for storing dates and times.
The Total column in the database is of type DECIMAL(10,2).
I'm not using any custom transformations or converters that could affect the data before serialization.

I'm not sure what else to try to resolve this issue. Any help or suggestions would be greatly appreciated.
Thanks in advance!
closing:
JxA= is 0x2710 in hex (renders as '\x10) but 10,000 when converted from base64 to base10. Then shift the decimal place by two to get the original column value. Here's python code, but the process should be the same in any language.
import base64
import decimal
byte_string = base64.b64decode("JxA=")
decimal_int = int.from_bytes(byte_string, byteorder='big')
result = decimal.Decimal(decimal_int) / 100  # 100.00

topic: Can Apache Camel Postgresql Debezium Component Output Cloud Events
opening: Debezium connectors can be configured to output cloud events instead of the default Struct object. closing:
Apparently, I misread the component documentation. The Camel Debezium components can return a Struct or a Map. From the component doc:

By default, the component will emit the events in the body and
CamelDebeziumBefore header as Struct data type, the reasoning behind this, is to
perceive the schema information in case is needed. However, the component as well
contains a Type Converter that converts from default output type of Struct to Map
in order to leverage Camel’s rich Data Format types which many of them work out
of box with Map data type.

I ended up using the connect image provided by debezium, since this image already includes the connectors and some base configuration, which is more convenient to use than building my own image or installing the connector on the fly with docker compose.

I removed the host networking mode and replaced it with an extra network.

Your bootstrap server is wrong (try without an env file, and you do not need to mount that as a volume)

topic: How to reset Debezium offset to start streaming from different DB server after migration
opening:
We are using Debezium connectors to stream PostgreSQL data into kafka. We will have a major version upgrade on PostgreSQL(13 to 16) by side by side approach using logical replication to new server. After the upgrade we would like to continue streaming to kafka without reinitialising the data using snapshot. If I simply change connector properties to new server it will search for a WAL position to resume which is not available in new server.
Is there any way to reset offset or WAL position in debezium to follow new server and start streaming afterwards ?
closing: This can be achieved by renaming or creating a new connector and specifying snapshot.mode="never". Offset works based on connector name.

topic: Postgres CDC failure and WAL filling up disk space?
opening:
Suppose a CDC data loading tool (Fivetran, Airbyte, Debezium, etc) gets into a failure state and is not successfully running its incremental syncs of a Postgres data source. Also suppose that max_slot_wal_keep_size is set to -1. As far as I can tell, this means that the amount of WAL retained for the tool's replication slot will be allowed to grow without bounds.
My question: assuming the tables continue to grow, is the end state of this scenario that the WAL eventually fills up all disk space, causing total catastrophe for the production database? Does the answer depend on whether the tool is pointed at read-only replica of the database?
closing: If you configure PostgreSQL to retain all WAL required for logical decoding, and the progress of logical decoding is stalled, the disk will eventually fill up and PostgreSQL will crash. To prevent that from happening, there is the parameter max_slot_wal_keep_size, which will make PostgreSQL abandon the replication rather than die.

Yep, if max_slot_wal_keep_size = -1 and the CDC tool is stuck, WAL will keep growing until it fills up disk—can totally bring down the primary. Using a read replica doesn’t help; WAL still piles up on the primary. Always monitor replication slots or set a limit to avoid surprises.

topic: How to define timestamp in Flink SQL based on Kafka connector with Avro format
closing:

closing:
The error is caused by a mismatch between the field value and what is expected in the schema. The value you're providing for the "total" field is "b****@g****.com" which is a string. However, your schema requires that this field is either "double" or "null".
You can find the error message in the log you shared:

```

    at org.apache.avro.generic.GenericDatumWriter.writeField(GenericDatumWriter.java:247)

```

```

    "subject": "gkp.order_production.orders-value",
    ...
    \"fields\":[
        ...
        {\"name\":\"total\",\"type\":[\"double\",\"null\"]},
}

```

Make sure you're assigning the correct data type to the total field before publishing it to the topic.

The way AvroConnector works by default is that the order of fields defined in the schema should be the same as the order in which the columns appear in the data. Once I configured this, the connector began to work as expected. Or simply, I configured "auto.register.schemas" as True and added the necessary columns in "field.include.list" property in the same orders in which they appear in my Postgres table. This worked for me.

closing:
you are not hitting a limitation with running two connectors against the same Oracle database. The problem happens because Kafka Connect is timing out during configuration validation.
When you create a connector, the Connect worker performs a full validation step. It tries to connect to the Oracle database and also checks access to Kafka or Event Hubs for the internal schema history topic. If either of these steps is slow or unreachable from the worker, the REST request times out even though the worker is still running the validation in the background.
To fix this, check that the Connect worker can reach both Oracle and the Kafka or Event Hubs endpoints from its network environment. Make sure database service names, listeners, and firewall rules are correct. Also confirm that the schema history topic can be created or accessed with the credentials provided.
If validation still takes too long, you can increase the timeout values for the schema history operations.
When running more than one connector against the same Oracle database, make sure each connector uses a unique topic prefix and its own schema history topic name. This prevents conflicts between connectors and ensures each instance maintains separate metadata.
In short, the timeout does not mean you cannot run multiple connectors. It only indicates that validation could not complete due to a slow or blocked network path. Once connectivity and timeouts are adjusted, the second connector will register normally.

topic: Google Cloud PubSub Synchronous Pull: Getting One Message at a Time Instead of Batches
opening:
Problem
I'm using Google Cloud PubSub with synchronous pull and ordering enabled to consume messages from a Debezium Server setup, but I'm only receiving one message at a time instead of getting messages in batches, which is severely impacting performance.
I understand that with ordering enabled, there can only be one outstanding batch at a time per ordering key to maintain message order. However, does "batch" in this context mean just 1 message at a time? Shouldn't I still be able to pull multiple messages in a single synchronous pull request, even with ordering constraints?
My Consumer Configuration:
# Example Python consumer
from google.cloud import pubsub_v1

subscriber = pubsub_v1.SubscriberClient()
subscription_path = subscriber.subscription_path(project_id, subscription_name)

# Current approach - getting one message at a time
def synchronous_pull():
    response = subscriber.pull(
        request={
            "subscription": subscription_path,
            "max_messages": 100,  # Expecting multiple messages
        }
    )
    
    # But response.received_messages only contains 1 message!
    print(f"Received {len(response.received_messages)} messages")  # Always prints 1

What I've Tried:

Increased max_messages to 100, 500, 1000 (still getting 1 message)
Adjusted PubSub batching settings on publisher side[debezium side]

Constraints:

Must use synchronous pull (cannot use asynchronous/streaming pull due to application architecture)
Need to process messages in batches for efficiency

Question
Why is Google Cloud PubSub synchronous pull only returning one message at a time despite setting max_messages to a higher value? How can I configure synchronous pull to receive multiple messages in a single request?
closing:
The per-ordering key batch sizes for synchronous Pull can be up to max_messages, but can be smaller. The pull batch size depends on many factors including pull rate, backlog size, and, in the case of subscribing with ordering enabled, the number of ordering keys. However, even when there are a lot of messages available, they are not all guaranteed to be returned on a pull request because Pub/Sub tries to balance returning more messages with minimizing end-to-end latency.
In the specific code sample provided, there isn't any code for acknowledging messages once they have been pulled, so any messages delivered in the initial batch will expire (default acknowledgement deadline is 10 seconds), which will trigger redelivery. When redelivering messages for a subscription with ordering enabled, Pub/Sub has no guarantees on what messages will be in the redelivered batch, just that the first published un-acknowledged message will be first in the batch.
From some testing with your code sample, without any acknowledgement logic, I found that what tends to happen is over time, batches begin to only contain 1 message per-ordering key. However, if you begin acknowledging messages, you may start to see larger message batches.
If you always require larger message batches, you can consider acknowledging messages and buffering them within your subscriber client in order to receive more messages, later processing the messages as a batch when you have received enough. Note that acknowledging the messages will prevent them from being redelivered if the batch processing fails.
Another recommendation would be to process your messages asynchronously so that you can have many outstanding pull requests to increase your throughput, as is suggested in the documentation. If you have some executor (like a ThreadPoolExecutor), then you can use the asynchronous client to issue pull requests in a loop and process asynchronously like (based on this sample):
client = pubsub_v1.SubscriberAsyncClient()

topic: Setup Kafka Consumers to process Debezium snapshot before current events
opening:
I am working with Java/Spring/Kafka on a new system that will consume events from both compacted topics and standard non compacted CDC topics. The events on these topics are published by a Debezium Postgres Connector. The connector has a snapshot.mode: never for production.
Goals:

I want my consumers to process snapshot data on startup, and continue to process current events after that.
Ideally, I would like this to be idempotent, re-runnable in future if needed and not limited to an initial state backfill action.

Constraints:

The consumers will be processing these events and persisting into a temporal table.
Initiating an adhoc snapshot could have impacts to other teams that do not have idempotent consumers for processing events from the same topics.

Initial thoughts:

Use Debezium signal table to execute a snapshot command in production.
Downside -> Would require a lot of collaboration with multiple teams and may significantly impact timeline.
Create a new Debezium Connector and topic, specific for my use case. Have my consumers subscribe to the new topic first, then, when the backfill is complete, switch back to the official topics for current events.
Downside -> This would involve a time difference in between topic subscription change and the offsets from the first topic to the next may cause issues (honestly not sure here).
Create a new Debezium Connector and topic for this purpose. Set the snapshot.mode: initial_only and have it configured to send an event indicating the snapshot is complete. Programmatically update the consumers to consume from 2 topics, prioritizing the snapshot topic. When the complete event is consumed, start processing from the current event topic.
Upside -> No downtime or manual intervention.
Downside -> Increased complexity and may not follow best practices for this kind of use case.

I am not an expert on Debezium and how Kafka operates with tracking offsets etc, so any advice on another approach/update to one of the above would be fantastic.
closing:
I would advise against trying to handle this by stitching two sets of topics together. This will be very error-prone and will likely yield situations of duplicates or data loss if offset positions are mismanaged.
The simpliest approach is to setup 2 independent pipelines, the first is your existing pipeline where you stream changes without backfill events to consumers that only want those events. Your second pipeline would be a new source connector with a separate set of topics that consumers support backfill, idempotent operations consume. This avoids any potential errors.
This has the added benefit that if you do perform any backfill operations (whether adhoc blocking or initial snapshots), capturing changes on the tables do not suffer latency for consumers that are uninterested in backfill events.
If you'd really rather have a single source pipeline and a single set of topics, this can be achieved, but it requires the use event filtering for it to work.

Topics are populated with all events, r from initial or adhoc snapshots, c, u, and d from the streaming of changes from the WAL.

Consumers that do not support backfill events would include the Filter transform in the transformation chain where you would exclude op=r events. This means that any initial, incremental, or blocking snapshot event will never be consumed by that consumer.


In my humble opinion, space is cheap and separate pipelines provides not only some flexibility, but it also keeps the two independent and isolated, avoiding situations where a problem with one does not directly affect the other consumers.
But the latter keeps things scaled to a single pipeline and a single set of topics, at the expense of extra complexity and little overhead to filter unwanted events from consumers that don't want r events.

topic: Capture Oracle metadata via Debezium connector
opening:
I'm sourcing Oracle data into Kafka topics using Debezium Oracle connector.
I have a source Oracle table, as below:

```
CREATE TABLE MYDATA.MY_USER
(
  USER_ID           RAW(16) DEFAULT SYS_GUID() NOT NULL,
  FIRST_NAME        VARCHAR2(100) NOT NULL,
  ...
  CONSTRAINT "PK_MY_USER" PRIMARY KEY (USER_ID)
);
COMMENT ON TABLE MYDATA.MY_USER '{"tags.category": "Personal", "description": "User  master data."}';
COMMENT ON COLUMN MYDATA.MY_USER.DOB IS '{"tags.category": "PII", "description": "User date of birth."}';

```

Now, I'd like these metadata values (COMMENT ON properties) to be carried over by Debezium along with Change Data Capture, so that I can access data as well as metadata from the Kafka topic.  Can you help me achieve this?  Do you know the Debezium connector properties that can help achieve this?
Ref: https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/oracle.html
closing:
While Debezium does support the capture of comments on tables and columns for some databases, the Debezium Oracle connector does not provide support for these at this time. This is primarily driven by several key aspects of schema tracking that would need to be adjusted:

Oracle comments are performed using supplemental COMMENT ON SQL statements, and cannot be included as part of the CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE statements. Such statements are not seen as DDL changes of interest and are ignored.

The connector relies on using the DBMS_METADATA.GET_DDL procedure, does not return comments that are associated with columns, which is problematic since CREATE TABLE cannot include comment clauses, as outlined in point 1, unlike other databases do.


Unlike comments, Oracle's new annotation syntax is another way to set metadata on columns and tables, and this aligns more closely with your use case. These should be captured as the DDL syntax for CREATE TABLE and ALTER TABLE support these.

topic: Understanding Debezium Snapshot
opening:
Debezium’s PostgreSQL snapshot docs note :

always
The connector performs a snapshot every time that it starts. The snapshot includes the structure and data of the captured tables. Specify this value to populate topics with a complete representation of the data from the captured tables every time that the connector starts. After the snapshot completes, the connector begins to stream event records for subsequent database changes.

Let’s say the following happens:

Snapshot begins.
New row is inserted
Snapshot ends
Stream from latest

Will row 2’s message still be handled by Debezium or it may be skipped?
closing:
The snapshot will not contain that row so it will only come up later, in streaming.
Debezium snapshot procedure begins with opening a transaction and by default, the snapshot.isolation.mode is serializable which behaves the same as repeatable read in terms of visibility of concurrent changes. As a result, the newly inserted row isn't visible to the snapshot.
If you change the mode to read committed (or read uncommitted but it'll just do the same thing in Postgres) there is some risk of inconsistencies Debezium doc warns about in the description of read committed:

minor data inconsistencies can occur when a record is added during the initial snapshot, and the connector later recaptures the record after the streaming phase begins

Still, their description of the anomaly sounds like it'd somehow get processed twice in that scenario, not skipped.

topic: Debezium SQL Server v2: Best practices for handling Schema Namespace fragmentation across multiple DB shards (SpecificRecord issue)
opening:
I am looking for advice on how to handle Avro schema namespaces when ingesting data from multiple identical SQL Server databases (sharding scenario) using the Confluent FullyManaged SQL Server Connector v2.
The Scenario: We have N databases with identical schemas (e.g., ShardedDB_01, ShardedDB_02…) writing to the same Kafka topics. In our legacy pipeline (Connector v1), the default behavior produced a uniform namespace for all records, regardless of the physical source database. This allowed our Java Consumers to simply use SpecificRecord with a single generated avsc class for all incoming messages, without any custom configuration.
The Problem with v2: The Debezium v2 connector now generates schemas where the database name is hardcoded into the namespace by default:

Source A: my.prefix.ShardedDB_01.dbo.MyTable

Source B: my.prefix.ShardedDB_02.dbo.MyTable


Even though the fields are identical, Schema Registry treats these as completely different schemas/namespaces.
The Impact: Because of this fragmentation, we cannot use the standard SpecificDeserializer anymore. The consumer expects a specific class (e.g., com.mycompany.avro.MyTable), but receives records with schemas pointing to dynamic, DB-specific namespaces. We are forced to fallback to GenericRecord, losing type safety, which is a significant regression from our v1 experience.
My Questions:

Source Side (Normalization): Is there a native Debezium v2 configuration or a standard SMT pattern to exclude the Database Name from the namespace (restoring the v1-like uniform behavior: my.prefix.dbo.MyTable)?


Note: We attempted a recursive custom SMT to rewrite the namespace, but traversing Debezium’s complex, deep structures (before/after structs) proved to be too memory-intensive, causing OOM errors on high-throughput workers.


Consumer Side: If normalization at the source is not possible, how do you handle SpecificRecord deserialization in a sharded v2 scenario? Is there a standard way to map multiple writer schemas to a single reader schema without maintaining N duplicate POJOs?

Any help to restore the “uniform schema” capability would be greatly appreciated.
Thanks!

topic: Debezium + Transaction Outbox in Spring Boot: how to avoid duplicate Kafka events with CDC when reprocessing and multiple consumers?
opening:
I’m implementing the Transaction Outbox pattern using Debezium CDC in a Spring Boot microservice and I’m struggling with duplicate event semantics in failure and reprocessing scenarios.
Tech stack:

Spring Boot 3.x

Spring Data JPA

PostgreSQL 14

Debezium PostgreSQL connector

Kafka

Multiple Kafka consumer groups

No custom outbox publisher (Debezium only)



Database schema

```
CREATE TABLE orders (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  status VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
  total_amount NUMERIC NOT NULL,
  updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE outbox_event (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  aggregate_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
  aggregate_id UUID NOT NULL,
  event_type VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  payload JSONB NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_outbox_created_at ON outbox_event(created_at);

```

The orders row and the outbox_event row are inserted in the same database transaction.

Spring service code

```
@Transactional
public void confirmOrder(UUID orderId) {
    Order order = orderRepository.findById(orderId)
        .orElseThrow();

    order.confirm();

    OutboxEvent event = new OutboxEvent(
        UUID.randomUUID(),
        "Order",
        order.getId(),
        "OrderConfirmed",
        objectMapper.writeValueAsString(order)
    );

    orderRepository.save(order);
    outboxRepository.save(event);
}

```


Debezium configuration (simplified)

```
{
  "connector.class": "io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector",
  "database.hostname": "postgres",
  "database.port": "5432",
  "database.user": "cdc",
  "database.password": "cdc",
  "database.dbname": "orders_db",
  "database.server.name": "orders-service",
  "table.include.list": "public.outbox_event",
  "tombstones.on.delete": "false",
  "transforms": "outbox",
  "transforms.outbox.type": "io.debezium.transforms.outbox.EventRouter",
  "transforms.outbox.route.by.field": "aggregate_type",
  "transforms.outbox.table.field.event.key": "aggregate_id",
  "transforms.outbox.table.field.event.payload": "payload"
}

```

Each outbox row is transformed into a Kafka message via Debezium’s EventRouter.

Problem
Under certain conditions, duplicate logical events appear in Kafka:

Debezium restarts or connector rebalances

Kafka topic retention causes consumers to replay

Consumers reset offsets for reprocessing

Multiple consumer groups consume the same topic


Even though:

The outbox write is transactional

Each outbox row has a unique UUID

Kafka message key is set to aggregate_id


Kafka idempotent producers don’t apply here since Debezium is the producer.

Observed behavior

The same outbox_event.id can appear more than once in Kafka when:

Debezium replays WAL segments

Snapshots or connector restarts occur



This leads to duplicated side effects unless consumers implement deduplication.



Questions

Is it expected behavior that Debezium can re-emit the same outbox row after restarts or offset resets?

Is consumer-side deduplication (based on outbox_event.id) considered mandatory when using Debezium Outbox?

Are there recommended ways to:

Prevent re-emission at the Debezium level?

Or safely mark outbox rows as “processed” without breaking CDC guarantees?



Should the Kafka message key be:

aggregate_id

outbox_event.id

or a composite key?



How do production systems typically balance:

replayability

consumer reprocessing

and avoiding duplicate side effects?




I’m looking for real-world guidance, not just theoretical guarantees.
closing:
I'll try to answer your questions, but first I must say the lead-up to your questions is a bit confusing. For example:

Under certain conditions, duplicate logical events appear in Kafka:

What do you mean by "duplicate logical events"? As in, what does the "logical" qualifier mean? What's the difference between a logical duplicate and a duplicate?


Kafka topic retention causes consumers to replay


The retention causes consumers to replay? How? Can you elaborate?


Consumers reset offsets for reprocessing


If you reprocess, surely you expect to see events you have processed previously again, right? So what's the problem?


Multiple consumer groups consume the same topic


Consumer groups operate independently of each other, offsets are committed per consumer group. What are you trying to achieve - that if an offset is committed for one consumer group, it should be committed for any? How would you then have different services consume the same topics?

The same outbox_event.id can appear more than once in Kafka when:
[..]
This leads to duplicated side effects unless consumers implement deduplication.

Your consumers should definitely implement deduplication, unless your events are naturally idempotent.
There are many scenarios that can lead to duplicate publishing, and even if you where to set up your system so that events are produced and delivered exactly once, you still wouldn't have implemented exactly-once-processing. Your consumer could crash after an event was processed, but before the offset was committed, so you'd still get duplicates. Always implement an "idempotent consumer".
Maybe that's the solution to your problem, if you do that, the intrinsics of Debezium might become less important.
Now to your questions:

Is it expected behavior that Debezium can re-emit the same outbox row after restarts or offset resets?

Not sure, but I'd say probably yes. While writing to the outbox (and WAL) is transactional, publishing to Kafka is not.

Is consumer-side dedu

Debezium (and CDC in general) is at-least-once, not exactly-once. So seeing the same outbox_event.id more than once is expected behavior in your setup.
In your case (Postgres + WAL + EventRouter), Debezium:

Reads WAL via logical replication

Publishes change events to Kafka

Commits offsets asynchronously


If the connector crashes after emitting but before offset commit, it will resume from the last committed LSN and may re-emit events. Rebalances and offset resets have the same effect. This is normal for Kafka Connect–based pipelines.
Even if Debezium never re-emitted anything, you would still need idempotent consumers. A consumer can:
1   Process the event
2 Apply the side effect
3 Crash before committing the offset
On restart, the event is delivered again. Exactly-once delivery does not imply exactly-once processing.
Because of that, trying to eliminate duplicates at the Debezium layer is usually the wrong goal. CDC pipelines are designed for durability and replayability. The place where correctness must be enforced is the consumer.
In production systems, consumer-side idempotency is standard practice. Typical approaches:

Maintain a processed_events table keyed by outbox_event.id

Use idempotency keys for external integrations

Prefer state-setting logic (e.g., “set status = CONFIRMED”) over imperative side effects


For example:

```
CREATE TABLE processed_events (
  event_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  processed_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT now()
);

```

On consume:

Attempt to insert event_id

If it already exists → skip

Otherwise → apply business logic


Regarding the Kafka key:

aggregate_id preserves ordering per aggregate (most common choice)

outbox_event.id helps with dedup identity but breaks per-aggregate ordering


A common production setup is:

Kafka key = aggregate_id

Event ID = outbox_event.id (payload or header for dedup)


Finally, outbox rows are typically treated as immutable. Marking them as “processed” often creates additional CDC noise and complexity

topic: Enable TRACE logs on debezium
opening: how can I enable trace logs in Debezium version 3.0.8.Final? I tried enabling them using log4j2 and a .properties file. Is there anything else I can try?
closing:
I've enabled Debezium Oracle Source connector trace logs with this:
curl -s --user user:pass -X PUT -H "Content-Type:application/json" http://<connect_host>:<connect_port>/admin/loggers/io.debezium.connector.oracle -d '{"level": "DEBUG"}'
You can go with DEBUG, WARN or TRACE. Set to INFO if you want to make it as default.
You need to do this for every kafka connect host in a cluster.
